newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland gives go-ahead to shipbuilding group.
newsitem.headline: Poland gives go-ahead to shipbuilding group.

text.p: Poland has approved a plan to form a new holding group in which shipyards, their suppliers and banks will join forces against foreign competition.
Privatisation Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek told a news conference the holding group, which will be led by Stocznia Szczecinska SA, would be set up by the end of this year.

Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz, who attended a meeting of top government officials, industry heads and bankers in the western port city of Szczecin, pledged government support for the group which would be built around the Szczecin shipyard.
Members could include the Stocznia Gdynia shipyard, the H Cegielski engine maker from the western city of Poznan, the Huta Czestochowa steel mill, several banks and companies, he said.

"The government expects from the companies a detailed plan of the holding's development with a timetable....The shipbuilding industry must have a future and the government is offering far-reaching help in its creation," he said.

Last year the Polish shipbuilding industry, burdened with debts and hit by a strong zloty, made an aggregate loss of $7 million despite a flood of orders. Szczecin yard, a notable exception, just broke even on $460 million sales.
Kaczmarek said the holding's creation would begin with Szczecin and Gdynia shipyards, establishing equity links. It would later be grouped with Cegielski.
The plan might involve breaking up state-owned Cegielski into two firms with one producing ship engines entering the holding and the remainder operating separately, he said.
Cimoszewicz said the government did not rule out foreign participation in the group. But there were no proposals so far.
